title: How Can a Socio-political Conflict Speak? Some Trends in the Study of West Bengal’s Naxalbari Movement, 1967–1972
note: Vanessa Corrado’s article in The Lab’s Quarterly, vol. XXIII, no. 2 (2021), pp. 59–82. The issue is dated April–June 2021 and states that the journal uses double-blind peer review. Corrado combines historiographical review with oral research; the article describes a 25 May 1967 police firing at Bengai Jote but presents some preceding events through a 2019 former activist’s oral account.
whyItMatters: The article locates the movement’s rural origins and traces the formation of revolutionary committees and the CPI (ML) in Calcutta. Its account of the firing and its causes partly draws on a named former activist’s oral narration, so those details need attribution.
